text.title: 垃圾桶旁的最后一站
text.situation:
离开前，乔问哪个桶用于回收瓶子。露丝指向当地分类标志，没有凭瓶子的颜色猜测。示意图显示未回收废物可能进入填埋。玛雅在包装上看到可生物降解，但露丝提醒分解取决于条件，不意味着能乱扔。另一块展板用不可生物降解垃圾指不易自然分解的废物。她们核对标签，让地面保持干净，方便下一批访客。

乔：这个瓶子可以在这里回收吗？
露丝：读桶旁的标志，它说明这项收集接受什么。
玛雅：可降解意味着能把包装留地上吗？
露丝：不能，要用正确收集点。

paragraphs.en: Before leaving, Jo asked which container was used to recycle bottles. Ruth pointed to a local sorting sign rather than guessing from the bottle’s colour. A diagram showed that waste not recovered might go to landfill. On a packet, Maya read biodegradable, but Ruth reminded her that breaking down depends on conditions and does not make littering acceptable. Another panel used the phrase non-biodegradable trash for waste that does not readily break down naturally. They checked the labels and left the ground clear for the next visitors.

paragraphs.en:
Jo: Can this bottle be recycled here?
Ruth: Read the sign beside the bin. It tells you what this collection accepts.
Maya: Does biodegradable mean I can leave the packet on the ground?
Ruth: No. Use the correct collection point.
